title: link channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.link.channel.v2). Same convention as afbws.alarm.channel.v2: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.link.<op>.v2`, no .request/.response/.push suffixes); the same schema is the request, its response (echoes `request_id`) and the server push (no `request_id`). Collections are arrays (`items[]`, `ids[]`), so bulk operations are single messages; per-element failures come back in `rejected[]` (only with `request_id`), a whole-request failure is `afbws.link.error.v2`. Config records are afbws.link.user.v1 / afbws.link.admin.v1 (role-chosen by the backend); runtime status records (`afbws.link.state.v2`, `status` operation) are separate and never mixed into config items. Pushes are deltas: list/set push = upsert by `bf_id`, delete push = removal, status push = only changed statuses (repeated heartbeats without change are silent). See AFB/docs/ws/link.md.

entity.description: Role-chosen config view — afbws.link.user.v1 (non-manager, including the synthetic virtual pseudo-connector) or afbws.link.admin.v1 (manager). The backend chooses which, never the client.

setInput.description: Role-chosen set() item shape — the backend selects which by the authenticated caller's role, never by a client-declared schema id. anyOf, not oneOf: neither shape carries a discriminating `schema` field, and a minimal payload (e.g. {bf_id, dry_run}) is structurally valid under both. The backend, not this schema, decides which fields a given caller may actually use.

session.title: Live session.hello capabilities — display-only, not persisted config.

dry_run.description: Effective value for this session (AFB override if set, else BF's own).

statusItem.title: link runtime status record (AFB-only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
statusItem.description: Runtime-only BF status — never carries name/broker/ACL/keys/policy/config, see link.user.v1.json/link.admin.v1.json for that. `updated_at` is the moment of the LAST STATE CHANGE (connected, heartbeat_stale, broker/daemon/session state), NOT of the last heartbeat: repeated session.heartbeat without any change neither move `updated_at` nor produce a push. There are no heartbeat timestamp/interval fields — the client only needs `heartbeat_stale`. `daemon` is null until the first daemon.status after connect; `session` is null whenever `connected` is false (disconnect resets both).

heartbeat_stale.description: AFB-derived stale flag (no heartbeat within 3x the negotiated interval).

updated_at.description: ISO timestamp of the last change of this status record (not of the last heartbeat).

rejection.title: One element that was not applied by set/delete/pair/restart.
rejection.description: `item` (the current authoritative record) is only allowed with code `conflict`.

list.title: afbws.link.list.v2 — read connectors (request / response / server push).
list.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): optional `scope` (usable = default, working accounts the caller may trade on incl. virtual; admin = full registry as admin views, managers only) and `ids[]` filter (none = all of the scope). Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` (afbws.link.user.v1 | afbws.link.admin.v1, role-chosen). Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): `items[]` (at least one) created/changed connectors — upsert by `bf_id`, never a snapshot; removal is `afbws.link.delete.v2` push. The first list/status request subscribes the connection to link pushes. There is no separate `get`: use `ids`.

set.title: afbws.link.set.v2 — create/update connectors (request / response / server push).
set.description: Request (`request_id`, no `rejected`): `items[]` of role-chosen set input, at least one. Response (same `request_id`, `rejected` present): applied `items[]` (authoritative records, possibly empty) + `rejected[]` (per-item failures; `conflict` carries the current `item`). Push (no `request_id`): `items[]` (at least one) created/changed on the server's own initiative — upsert by `bf_id`; `rejected` is not allowed.

delete.title: afbws.link.delete.v2 — delete connectors (request / response / server push).
delete.description: Request (`request_id`, no `rejected`): `ids[]`, at least one. Response (same `request_id`, `rejected` present): `ids[]` actually removed (possibly empty) + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): `ids[]` (at least one) removed from the registry — drop by `bf_id`; `rejected` is not allowed.

pair.title: afbws.link.pair.v2 — start/restart pairing (request / response).
pair.description: Request: `ids[]`, at least one (manager or owner; the virtual connector is rejected with `unsupported_action`). Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` — one `{id, item, pairing_string, expires_at}` per started pairing + `rejected[]`. No server push.

restart.title: afbws.link.restart.v2 — restart BF daemons (request / response).
restart.description: Request: explicit `ids[]`, at least one — never implicitly picks the first accessible BF. Response (same `request_id`): `ids[]` for which the restart command was sent + `rejected[]`. No server push.

status.title: afbws.link.status.v2 — runtime statuses (request / response / server push).
status.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): optional `ids[]` (none = every connector visible in the caller's usable view). Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` of status records (afbws.link.state.v2). Push (no `request_id`): `items[]` (at least one) of ONLY the statuses that changed — repeated heartbeats without a state change produce no push. `updated_at` of a record is the moment of its last state change. The first list/status request subscribes the connection to pushes.

error.title: afbws.link.error.v2 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).
error.description: Per-element failures of a batched operation are reported in that response's `rejected[]`, not here. `code` is the closed common errorCode set.
